text: Four lessons ago this was a kickoff meeting's worth of stakeholder complaints. Now it's a real implementation, built decision by decision against Caldwell Precision Manufacturing's own requirements. This lesson reviews what that build actually covers against the CIS-ITSM certification's own domains, and names what this course deliberately left for Course 9.

Incident Management showed up as a Priority Lookup Rule and targeted routing, not a vague promise to work faster. Problem Management showed up as the Line 3 printer case, and the exam-relevant lesson there is pace: Problem is supposed to be slower than Incident, by design, because it's chasing a permanent cause instead of a fast workaround. Change Enablement showed up as a risk value calculated from real, checkable answers, driving approval automatically instead of sitting there as a label nobody acts on.

Request Management showed up as the New Hire catalog item's rollup status and two separate item-level SLAs, one per fulfillment team's own timeline. Knowledge Management showed up as a real Draft-to-Publication approval path and retirement discipline, not a shared document nobody updates. And Service Level Management showed up as Start, Pause, and Stop conditions plus a correctly chosen schedule for each priority tier — because a duration number alone never tells you what an SLA actually measured.

Look back and cmdb_ci shows up twice without ever being explained. Lesson 30's root_cause field pointed at a cmdb_ci record for the failing switch. And Change Risk Assessment asked whether a change touches a business-critical Configuration Item — exactly how Meridian's own risk got calculated. Both references did real work in this capstone. What a CMDB actually is, how a CI relationship gets modeled, and how Discovery populates that data automatically were never explained, on purpose.

That's the whole course, start to finish, and that's the honest gap it leaves open. Course 9, ServiceNow CMDB, CSDM and Discovery, picks up exactly where those two unexplained cmdb_ci references left off.
